added_lines: Annual Mass for Deceased Diocesan Clergy & Religious The Annual Mass for Deceased Diocesan Clergy and Religious will take place On: Tuesday 24th of November 2026 In: St Peter's Belfast At: 7:30pm In particular we remember and offer Mass for those who have died in this past year. All are welcome to join Bishop Alan McGuckian SJ as he celebrates this Mass. Save the date! All are invited to come and hear from representatives of 6 Christian Churches who will consider: 'Who is Mary in God’s Plan of Salvation?' Martina Purdy will present on behalf of the Roman Catholic tradition. There also will be time for audience questions, chai red by Alf McCreary ( Belfast Telegraph, BBC News) This is an opportunity to listen and understand other perspectives. Wednesday, 2 December 2026 at 7pm in Corr’s Corner Hotel, Newtownabbey. Refreshments will be served. To aid in planning please rsvp to

This time of year is the busiest for the foodbank. Winter and the extra demands of Christmas are approaching. Please remember the Foodbank can only accept non-perishable foods. Also, they do not accept presents. Leaflets are available in the Church porch with full details. Sadly it is often a time when stocks are at their lowest. As always thank you for your generous support. We would like to ask those who do not presently donate, to consider joining us. Every little helps. Thanky

Thursday 26th November - 7.00pm: The Straight Story An elderly man embarks on a remarkable journey across the American Midwest on a lawnmower to reconcile with his estranged brother. A gentle and moving pilgrimage that speaks of patience, forgiveness, and grace. Thursday 17th December - 7.00pm: The Holdovers Over the Christmas holidays, a group of lonely and mismatched individuals discover unexpected companionship and belonging. Warm, funny, and deeply humane, this is a story of healing, and hope. All are welcome, no need to register.
